correctness.rationale: The displayed Weyl action multiplies with phase exp(−iσ(z,w)/2), so conjugation of W_xi and of the character Toeplitz operator has the same eigencharacter. Irreducibility gives scalar proportionality. With the radial unit vector L_{k−1}(|w|²) and real a=|xi|, pairing with its shift leaves the tilt exp(a w) after multiplying the character. In the two-variable Laguerre generating integral the Gaussian quadratic coefficient is (1−st)/[(1−s)(1−t)], the linear coefficients are a/(1−t) and at/(1−t), and the constant is −a²t/(1−t). Gaussian integration gives (1−st)^−1 exp(−a²st/(1−st)), establishing every diagonal coefficient and the stated zero without a Fourier convention ambiguity. The phase-weighted Weyl matrix average has norm at most 1 and equals 1 on W_xi. Covariance and the translated disk substitution leave a bounded scalar times the zero character operator, plus an error tending to zero by dominated convergence: the disk symmetric-difference fraction tends to zero pointwise and is bounded by 2, and the test-vector product is integrable. This works for each fixed bounded symbol with no uniform symbol bound needed. Thus the lower bound is 1 for the full range, and the zero symbol attains it. Distance is unchanged under norm closure; norm continuity of Weyl conjugation on this shift follows from the eigencharacter. For BUC symbols the Toeplitz range lies in C_1 by covariance and the symbol sup-norm bound, so the proper-subset conclusion is valid. The Hermite STFT/Bargmann unitary in Abreu–Speckbacher Eq. (6.2) identifies the mask and Toeplitz sesquilinear forms by coordinate reflection/rescaling; the phase cancels. Time-frequency shifts correspond to Weyl shifts up to unimodular factors, which do not affect distance to the complex linear range. The argument requires the irreducible true level and a Laguerre root, not the full reducible sum or arbitrary frequencies.
